clauses.reason: The lead of EO 10733 amends section 3 of EO 10479 by striking "fifteen" and inserting "sixteen". Section 403 of EO 10925 provides that EO 10479, EO 10482 and EO 10733 "are hereby revoked, and the Government Contract Committee established by Executive Order No. 10479 is abolished." (the held text names "10733 of October 10, 1957 (22 F.R. 8135)"). Section 402 provides "This order shall become effective thirty days after its execution." EO 10925 was signed 1961-03-06, so the revocation took effect 1961-04-05 (actor: President Kennedy). The 1961-03-06 signing date is not used as the effective date.

Paragraph (b) as rewritten by EO 10733 (ten other members; Executive Vice Chairman to be designated) is part of the same amendment to EO 10479 section 3. It ended with the express revocation of EO 10733 by section 403 of EO 10925, effective thirty days after execution on 1961-03-06, i.e. 1961-04-05 (section 402). The Committee it described was abolished by the same sentence.

research_rationale:
EO 10733 (signed 1957-10-10, 22 FR 8135) does nothing but amend section 3 of EO 10479, which created the Government Contract Committee: it changes the preamble's "fifteen" to "sixteen" members and rewrites paragraph (b) to add an Executive Vice Chairman. Section 403 of EO 10925 (signed 1961-03-06; 26 FR 1977), whose text is held, names EO 10479, EO 10482, EO 10733 "(22 F.R. 8135)" and EO 10557, declares them "hereby revoked" and abolishes the Committee; section 402 makes EO 10925 effective thirty days after its execution, i.e. 1961-04-05 (the exclusive reading of 'thirty days after' is the same day). A Cruden regex search of the held texts for the number 10733 finds no later instrument other than EO 10925; the 1989 OFR table also records 'Revoked by EO 10925'. Both clauses of the order are therefore terminated on 1961-04-05 and the whole order ends on that date. Status proposal: no.

savings.reason: Section 403 of EO 10925 transfers all records and property of the Committee to the President's Committee on Equal Employment Opportunity, which winds up the Committee's outstanding affairs; no continuing independent command of EO 10733 survives, because the amendment's only subject (membership of the abolished Committee) is gone.
